newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour takes unprecented poll lead.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour takes unprecented poll lead.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has taken an unprecedented 26-percentage-point lead over the ruling Conservatives in the runup to a general election due before the end of May, a new opinion poll released on Thursday showed.
Pollsters Gallup said the addition of 11 points to Labour's lead since February meant that no governing party in history has ever been so far behind in the last weeks of a parliament.
The survey, being published in Friday's edition of the Daily Telegraph, showed Labour's support had risen to 54 percent, up five points on February.
The Conservatives have dropped six percentage points to 28 percent, the poll showed. The centrist Liberal Democrats took 12.5 percent, up 0.5 percentage points on February.
Three out of four people polled by Gallup said they believed that the government was "on its last legs."
Prime Minister John Major has to call an election no later than May 22. The Conservatives, in power since 1979, are bidding for their fifth general election victory in a row.
